Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

exist verb

also existence, still exist, be real, survive (of things)

classical

Cic. N. D. 1.44: esse igitur deōs cōnfitendum est
Cic. Top. 27: esse ea dīcō quae cernī tangīque possunt

sum, esse, fuī

verb, irregular, conjugation

be, exist

Latin needs no special verb: esse itself asserts existence (Lewis & Short: “Asserting existence, to be, exist, live”), and then often stands first: sunt quī Propertium mālint, there are people who prefer Propertius (Quint. 10.1.93).

Other words

  • exstō, exstāre — still exist, be extant (of letters, books, buildings)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.48: exstant epistulae et Philippī ad Alexandrum

    Properly “stand out”.

  • in rērum nātūrā esse — exist (in the world, in reality)

    also used · classical · Cic. Acad. 2.84: negās tantam similitūdinem in rērum nātūrā esse; Gai. Inst. 3.97a: rem quae in rērum nātūrā esse nōn potest, velut hippocentaurum

Examples

  • esse ea dīcō quae cernī tangīque possunt, ut fundum, aedēs, parietem …

    by things that exist I mean things that can be seen and touched, like a farm, a house, a wall …Cic. Top. 27

  • esse igitur deōs cōnfitendum est

    we must admit, then, that the gods existCic. N. D. 1.44

  • Exstant epistulae et Philippī ad Alexandrum …

    There still exist letters of Philip to Alexander …Cic. Off. 2.48

See also real, live.
